2607.23927.title: Reality Monitoring in Large Language Models: Self-Knowledge That Transforms with Conversation Memory
2607.23927.paper_summary: A conversational AI that cannot tell its own output from what a user said will treat its own mistakes as user-provided facts. In humans, this capacity is called reality monitoring, and its failures are linked to hallucinations, delusions, and confabulation, yet whether LLMs possess it remains untested. Here we show, across two experiments and six LLMs, that source attribution depends on how conversational memory is structured: ceiling accuracy for self-generated content under minimal memory demands reverses to a fragile external-item advantage once episodic delay removes that shortcut. Feedback exposes two failures: in some models, internal and external judgments swap; in others, accuracy improves while confidence decouples from correctness, dissociations invisible to existing benchmarks. Across models, this pattern implicates active, not aggregate, parameter count. This suggests that as AI systems take on autonomous, multi-turn roles, evaluating what they know is not enough: tracking where that knowledge came from may matter equally.
2607.23927.paper_summary_zh: 一個無法區分自己輸出與用戶所說內容的對話式人工智慧，將把自己的錯誤視為用戶提供的事實。在人類中，這種能力被稱為現實監控，其失敗與幻覺、妄想和虛構有關，但大型語言模型（LLMs）是否具備這種能力仍未經測試。在這裡，我們展示了在兩個實驗和六個LLMs中，來源歸因取決於對話記憶的結構：在最低記憶需求下，自我生成內容的準確性達到上限，但一旦情節延遲移除這一捷徑，則轉變為脆弱的外部項目優勢。反饋揭示了兩個失敗：在某些模型中，內部與外部判斷互換；在其他模型中，準確性提高，而信心與正確性脫鉤，這些解離在現有基準中是不可見的。在各模型中，這一模式涉及的是主動的，而不是總體的參數計數。這表明，隨著人工智慧系統承擔自主的多輪角色，評估它們所知的內容並不足夠：追蹤這些知識的來源可能同樣重要。
